key_insight: The Blueprint proposes preparing DOE to deploy fault-tolerant quantum computers for scientific use beginning in 2028 and scale capabilities through the 2030s.
engineering_relevance: Integrating quantum computers into national scientific computing infrastructure requires coordinated development of error-corrected hardware, programming tools, system software, and facility readiness.
method: Target first-generation systems with at least 100 logical qubits and 10,000–100,000 hard logical operations per scientifically relevant calculation.
Build FTQC programming competencies, system software, and deployment-ready facilities.
Invest in applications, algorithms, and logical architectures to enable production-scale systems.
evidence_signal: The abstract cites recent error-corrected logical-operation demonstrations and commercial hardware roadmaps as motivation, but reports no new benchmarks validating the proposed deployment targets.
watch_item: Scientific utility by 2028 remains a strategic goal, contingent on hardware scaling, reliable logical operations, and successful infrastructure integration.
